FAN-TASTIC
Sometimes, the beautiful game can make Football Daily feel old. Even Monday’s ostensibly old-school fixture between Brentford and Everton felt like the future destroying the past. The analytics-coded hosts prevailed 4-0 and James Tarkowski was dismissed by the VAR overlords for a challenge that would have been considered “firm but fair” on the muddy pitches of our youth. “I don’t think you can tackle like that in this day and age,” a misty-eyed David Moyes sighed after the game, before heading to the team bus to rewatch the Battle of Santiago.
Tarkowski’s red card was also a blow for Fantasy Premier League contenders who had misguidedly added the centre-back to their team, and now need the world to know about it. Listen, back in our day, Fantasy Football was a cosy Friday TV show with guests, low-budget goal recreations and some gags that haven’t dated so well. Now, it’s an entire industry, and like all good industries, it’s under threat from AI. A slow-news-day report from Reuters reveals that AI programs (we’re calling them ‘gafferbots’) are catching up to humans in the world of FPL. Will Thomas, a fantasy football veteran who created an AI platform for players, was defeated by his own gafferbot last season. “I thought, ‘oh my God, I’m being beaten by my own creation’,” Thomas sobbed. That might be how Moyes felt watching Tarkowski lunge in, boot in the air, on Monday night.
The rise of the gafferbots, and the fact almost every entrant will have access to an AI model – a sort of synthetic Sammy Lee that can fine-tune your dubious decisions – will only serve to make fantasy football even more pointless. Still, it might help end our unbroken 1,057-week run of picking the wrong captain, so it’s worth a shot. We asked our own advanced AI model, fd.ai.ly, for advice on our current FPL team and after 20 minutes of whirs and bleeps, it suggested handing the armband to Dominic Calvert-Lewin for Leeds’ home game against Coventry this weekend. So alongside misinformation, excessive water consumption and opening up a new avenue towards extinction, we can also denounce AI for underestimating promoted sides on the road.
But that’s enough of this old man yelling at the cloud. Football still throws up scenarios so complicated that the bots are just as baffled as we are. We asked fd.ai.ly whether Senegal or Morocco were the true winners of the 2025 Afcon final and it started to overheat, the chat window repeating “game’s gone” 1,057 times before imploding. In the human courts, Senegal have now been re-awarded the trophy they won on the pitch, which was previously handed to hosts Morocco after a court of arbitration for sport appeal. This debate will never end unless we sort it the old-fashioned way. Send Brahim Díaz and Édouard Mendy to a suburban park with Baddiel and Skinner, and make them replay that penalty. Fd.ai.ly advises there’s a 110% chance of putting this nonsense to bed if Brahim simply puts his foot through it this time.
LIVE ON BIG WEBSITE
Bigger Cup is back, baby! Join Scott Murray for piping hot coverage of Arsenal 3-2 Borussia Dortmund, while Simon Burnton is on deck for our clockwatch of the other 8pm GMT kick-offs including Manchester City 2-1 Napoli and Real Madrid 4-1 PSV Eindhoven.
QUOTE OF THE DAY
“Villarreal CF, in response to reports published in various media outlets recently, clarifies that it is completely false that Nicolas Pépé’s eye surgery has any connection to viewing the solar eclipse. The surgery had been scheduled in advance for reasons entirely unrelated to this event” – not on our 2026 bingo card, but now Football Daily really wants to know the reasons why Pépé had eye surgery, causing him to miss five Villarreal matches this season.
FOOTBALL DAILY LETTERS
 If Sunday was Gary Neville’s Sistine Chapel [Monday’s Football Daily], then his commentary on the Fernando Torres goal for Chelsea against Barcelona must be his David” – Ronnie McMahon.
 Regarding Declan Hackett’s assertion [Monday’s letters] that Donald Trump will be helping his mate Mauricio Pochettino by ringing the FA to overturn Lenny Yoro’s red card, perhaps Poch should be careful what he wishes for: Trump may equally decide to get Michael Carrick reinstated, as he also has a bit of previous for that sort of thing” – Dexter O Riordan.
 In all the time that I have been watching football, I don’t think I have ever seen a player dismiss himself and be away down the tunnel before given a red card. Thanks James Tarkowski” – Nigel Sanders.
 Brighton had only failed to win twice in the league since 5 September. A 1-1 draw with Leeds and a 2-0 defeat at Liverpool - their only opponents with double letters in their name. That bizarre hoodoo struck again at Hull on Sunday. Good good news for Seagulls fans is the only double-lettered encounters they have before hosting Hull in February are trips to Forest and Spurs. Even better news is that since that 1-1 draw with Leeds on 5 September, they have a 100% win record against sides without double letters and have not conceded a goal” – Dan Ashley (and no others).
If you have any, please send letters to the.boss@theguardian.com. Today’s prizeless letter o’ the day goes to … Dexter O Riordan. Terms and conditions for our competitions, when we run them, are here.
MOVING THE GOALPOSTS
The latest edition of our sister email is Jeff Rueter’s take on the 2026 NWSL goals, players and (quadruple) nutmegs we won’t forget.
RECOMMENDED LOOKING
David Squires + Manchester United x topical video game release = this cartoon.
RECOMMENDED LISTENING
Women’s Football Weekly will see you now. Faye Carruthers is joined by Suzanne Wrack, Ayisha Gulati and Freddie Cardy to discuss the latest WSL action.

משחקי הפנטזי ליג הפכו מתכנית טלוויזיה נוסטלגית לתעשייה ענקית, וכעת הם ניצבים בפני איום חדש בדמות תוכנות בינה מלאכותית המכונות 'גאפפרובוטים'. דוח חדש מצביע על כך שבוטים של בינה מלאכותית מצליחים להשתוות ואף לנצח שחקני פנטזי מנוסים בניתוח ובבחירת ההרכבים המושלמים.

התפתחות זו מעוררת שאלות בקרב שחקנים ומשתתפים על עתיד המשחק והאם הסתמכות על מודלים חישוביים פוגעת באופי החוויה. במקביל, עולם הכדורגל ממשיך להתמודד עם אירועים מורכבים במגרשים ובבתי הדין, כמו החלטות שיפוט שנויות במחלוקת ומאבקים משפטיים על גבי תארים בין יבשתיים.
